business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial CGI Visual Effects and 3D Character Animation

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (United States-derived common law blended with customary law; the Business Corporations Act 1990 is modeled on Delaware and New York corporate law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Amended Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (Title II economic provisions, effective 1 May 2004)
No standalone bilateral investment treaty (BIT) or double taxation avoidance agreement (DTAA) is presently in force for the Republic of the Marshall Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended (RMI BCA); Money Laundering Control Act 2005, as amended (MLCA); AML/CFT Regulations and directives issued by the RMI Banking Commission, which supervises licensed registered agents and functions as the Republic's financial regulatory authority; the Republic of the Marshall Islands is a member of the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Nominee_Friendly (beneficial ownership records are held confidentially by the licensed RMI registered agent, are not publicly searchable, and are accessible to the RMI Government, Banking Commission and law-enforcement authorities only upon lawful demand under the MLCA; nominee directors and shareholders are permitted)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the bio-data page of the passport of each proposed director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (issued by the competent apostille authority of the country of origin; for non-Hague Convention countries, consular legalization through the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of the Marshall Islands in Washington, D.C.)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original banker's reference letter or good-standing confirmation from the UBO's depository bank (dated within 90 days of submission)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depository bank of the individual or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where required by the registered agent's KYC policy; otherwise authenticated by bank seal and notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registry extract for every corporate shareholder in the UBO ownership chain up to the ultimate natural person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or licensed registered agent of the relevant foreign corporation's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuer's jurisdiction is a Convention state; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 90 days) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or depository bank, with notarization by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional character and background reference letter issued by a licensed attorney or certified public accountant who has known the UBO for at least two years
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Practicing attorney or certified public accountant licensed in a recognized jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Convention states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, signatories and beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI Sanctions List and the RMI domestic measures enforced by the Banking Commission. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified using the FATF definition; any PEP match triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening is repeated at account-opening and periodically thereafter (at minimum annually), with adverse-media review included in the standard AML/CFT risk assessment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Registrar of Corporations – corporate name reservation registry (Majuro); reservations are filed through licensed RMI registered agents and administratively processed by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations under the RMI Business Corporations Act 1990
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the statutory language of corporate names; names must be entirely in Latin-alphabet characters and may contain numerals, spaces, periods and the ampersand. The name must include 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company', 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation (Corp., Inc., Co., Ltd.), or a word of equivalent meaning in a foreign language, and must be distinguishable from every name already registered in the RMI registry. No local-script transliteration or indigenous-language suffix is required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Marshall Islands (where it implies official government affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed for successive 30-day periods by filing a renewal request with the Registrar through the licensed registered agent before expiry. On rejection, the applicant receives a written notice stating the grounds (e.g., deceptively similar to an existing name, or containing a prohibited token). Within 30 days of the rejection notice, the applicant may file a written reconsideration application through its registered agent, accompanied by: (i) a legal memorandum distinguishing the proposed mark from the conflicting name; (ii) a notarized letter of consent from the holder of the conflicting name, where applicable; or (iii) written approval from the relevant RMI Ministerial authority for sensitive tokens. The Registrar must issue a decision within 10 business days of receipt. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may commence judicial-review proceedings in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days of the denial, in accordance with the RMI Civil Procedure Rules.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permissible for this non-resident offshore structure. The Business Corporation must maintain a registered office and licensed registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, which will be the registered agent's physical street address in Majuro; the commercial 3D animation and VFX studio may operate entirely remotely from any global location using cloud rendering and distributed workstations, without any RMI employees, premises or local business presence. The corporation will be designated as a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation, and as long as it derives no RMI-source income it will remain outside the RMI tax net and outside the Foreign Investment Business License regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection below 5%). Unannounced inspections are not conducted for non-regulated, non-resident corporations absent specific triggers such as AML/CFT red flags, sanctions-list or PEP matches, regulatory complaints, or an international mutual-assistance request. Verification of compliance, where it occurs, is ordinarily directed at the licensed registered agent's records rather than at the applicant's offshore business premises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (USD 900-1,200 for low-risk non-resident corporations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per the MLCA registered-agent compliance standard

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening subscription for all directors, shareholders and UBOs
Pre-incorporation legal due-diligence review and corporate-structure memorandum (fixed legal fee)
Bank reference letter processing fee (per UBO depository bank tariff)
International courier for original notarized and legalized documents to the registered agent (Majuro or Washington, D.C.)
Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) assessment - waived, with legal confirmation that no FIBL is required for qualified non-resident offshore activity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, Title 24 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (24 MIRC), as amended; principally Sections 26-33 (incorporation, filing and Certificate of Incorporation), Section 39 (organization meeting and initial directors), Section 51 (consideration for shares), Section 52 (officers), and Sections 55-56 (registered office and registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Certificate of Incorporation issued upon approval)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The RMI Business Corporations Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital, no escrow account, and no capital deposit requirement. Under 24 MIRC Section 51, shares may be issued for cash, services, or property as the Board of Directors determines, and are fully paid upon receipt of such consideration; authorized capital is fixed in the Articles only for fee computation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Title 24 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code) is ratified, and the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations are approved.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the founding shareholder's subscription for the initial allotment of authorized shares is accepted, and the President and Secretary shall issue share certificates upon receipt of full consideration.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office at the resident registered agent's address, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, is adopted.

FURTHER RESOLVED, that the persons named in officer acceptance letters are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer, authorized to open and operate bank, Wise B2B and SWIFT settlement accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, RMI Corporate Registry (direct submission or through an authorized RMI registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search against the Registry's index of existing and reserved corporate names; submit a name reservation application stating the proposed English name with a permitted suffix (Corporation, Incorporated, Company, Limited, or abbreviations thereof); pay the search and reservation fee; the Registrar reserves the cleared name for 120 days pending filing of Articles.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter of the RMI registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on indistinguishability grounds, file an alternate name or obtain a written consent from the holder of the conflicting name; if the reservation lapses, reapply without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or RMI consular officer (acknowledgment of incorporator's signature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in English containing: the corporate name; registered office address in Majuro; registered agent name; a lawful purpose clause (may state 'any lawful act or activity' permitted under 24 MIRC); authorized share structure (e.g., 50,000,000 shares of US$0.01 par value or no-par shares); and the incorporator's name and address. The incorporator must sign before a notary or an RMI consular officer; each page numbered and the acknowledgment page notarially certified.
required_dossiers: Copy of incorporator's passport or certificate of good standing (if corporate incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the defective instrument and re-execute; if the notarial acknowledgment is deficient, re-notarize before a competent notary or RMI consular officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Payment with the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (e-filing accepted via authorized registered agents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation together with a transmittal letter and the registered agent's acceptance of appointment; pay the statutory filing fee of US$275 for authorized capital up to 25,000 shares (graded fees apply above that threshold under 24 MIRC Section 27); select standard processing (3 business days) or expedited same-day/24-hour service; upon approval, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the original filing date.
required_dossiers: Wire transfer confirmation or paid fee invoice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, cure by filing a certificate of correction or amended Articles under 24 MIRC Section 34; if refusal rests on improper grounds, apply to the High Court for a writ of mandamus compelling acceptance; no duplicate filing fee is payable where the initial statutory fee was collected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Initial Directors and Registered Agent Acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator (by unanimous written consent); registered agent (acceptance of office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes a written consent appointing one or more initial directors (natural persons; no RMI residency requirement). The registered agent's written acceptance is filed with the Registry, and the registered office is the agent's street address in Majuro. For a non-resident domestic corporation, the board may deliberate and act entirely by electronic communication or unanimous written consent.
required_dossiers: Consent of Incorporator to Action in lieu of First Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or the registered agent declines appointment, execute a substitute consent or a statement of change of registered agent and registered office under 24 MIRC Section 56 and file promptly with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the First Board Resolution (Organizational Consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (unanimous written consent in lieu of organizational meeting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial directors adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution covering: ratification of incorporation; acceptance of the founding shareholder's share subscription; adoption of the registered office and registered agent; appointment of the President, Secretary and Treasurer; authorization to open bank, Wise B2B and SWIFT settlement accounts; and designation of account signatories. The signed consent and the resolution are filed in the corporate minute book maintained at the registered agent's office.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If unanimity is not achievable, convene a formal board meeting on notice pursuant to the bylaws; resolutions may be adopted by majority vote with a quorum present.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Share Certificates and Opening of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue the share certificate or certificates to the founding shareholder against the consideration accepted by the board; record the shareholder name, number of shares, certificate number, issue date and consideration in the stock transfer ledger; open the corporate seal, minute book and share ledger; maintain corporate records at the principal executive office (outside the Marshall Islands) or with the registered agent, as the board directs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificates are lost, destroyed or mis-issued, the board may authorize replacement certificates upon receipt of an indemnity affidavit; ledger entries may be corrected by written board consent.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Office (Ministry of Commerce and Trade); Tax and Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance. Corporate filings are lodged electronically through licensed Registered Agents using the RMI Online Corporate Registry portal; business licenses are filed via the Business License Division, Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned non-resident Business Corporation procures its legal identity by filing Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations through a licensed registered agent. No income-tax TIN is issuable for foreign-source activity; the corporation obtains (i) a Certificate of Incorporation with an RMI registration number, (ii) an annual franchise tax receipt and Annual Report filing acknowledgement, and (iii) a Business License only if it conducts physical or local activity in the Marshall Islands. Non-resident domestic corporations deriving all income from outside the RMI are not required to obtain an income-tax file number or to file RMI income tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporation exempt from RMI gross income tax on offshore revenue; taxation limited to a fixed annual franchise tax (based on authorized share capital) plus the Annual Report fee.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None applicable. RMI law contains no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election. Entity classification follows statutory form: a Business Corporation is per se a taxable legal person only to the extent it derives RMI-source income; a non-resident company may voluntarily opt into resident tax treatment by carrying on business in the RMI (subjecting only RMI-source income to tax). The absence of an income tax treaty network eliminates treaty-based hybrid elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax (the RMI levies no general consumption tax; customs import duties are the sole indirect levy)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A - no VAT/GST registration threshold exists; a Business License (annual fee) is required only for entities with physical RMI business premises or local sales, and no turnover test applies. A non-resident 3D animation service exporter has no indirect-tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI does not mandate e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based reporting. Invoices are governed by general contract law and may be issued in any commercial format. Electronic customs declarations are used exclusively for physical merchandise through the RMI Customs Automated Manifest and Declaration system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable by statute: the RMI imposes no VAT/GST, and non-resident domestic corporations are outside RMI gross income tax on offshore service revenue. To definitively establish export treatment, the corporation must evidence that the animation/VFX services are performed and consumed wholly outside the RMI, the counterparty is a non-resident, and consideration is settled in foreign currency into a non-RMI account; no zero-rating claim or refund application is necessary.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certificate of Incorporation and Non-Resident Status Declaration (issued by the Registrar of Corporations)
Executed Service Agreement and Statement of Work (defining offshore performance and delivery of 3D animation/VFX assets)
Commercial Invoice and Delivery Note (scoped to services rendered entirely outside the RMI)
SWIFT MT103 / Wise B2B Inward Remittance Certificate (evidence of foreign-currency settlement)
RMI Annual Franchise Tax Receipt and Annual Report Filing Acknowledgment (demonstrating good standing)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT-export clawback mechanism in the RMI because no VAT exists. However, fraudulent certifications to the Registrar of Corporations (false non-resident declarations or facade incorporation) are punishable under the Business Corporations Act, including fines up to US$500 per violation and possible involuntary dissolution; operation of a business without a required local license attracts administrative penalties and license revocation. Internationally, if a foreign tax authority (e.g., US IRS CFC/Subpart F, EU ATAD or OECD Pillar Two) determines the RMI entity lacks economic substance, the tax exemption may be disregarded and offshore revenue clawed back in the shareholder's residence jurisdiction. Records should be retained for at least seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Marshall Islands (BMI), acting as the central bank and monetary authority for the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI uses the United States dollar (USD) as its official legal tender. Pursuant to the Compact of Free Association and the RMI Banking Act 1987, the BMI does not maintain restrictive exchange controls on current account transactions, capital account transactions, or profit remittances. Foreign-owned non-resident business corporations may remit dividends, royalties, and service fees abroad without prior BMI exchange control approval, provided remittance documentation satisfies the anti-money laundering (AML) and countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) requirements imposed under the RMI AML/CFT framework (as amended by the Banking (Amendment) Act 2013 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2014). The RMI currency board system ensures complete USD convertibility at parity, with no surrender, rationing, or split-rate mechanisms affecting current or capital account flows. Practical remittance hurdles are limited to correspondent bank due diligence, beneficiary bank sanctions screening, and compliance with the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions regimes, given the dollar-clearing nexus.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in the RMI. Since the USD is the domestic currency and the RMI maintains a quasi-currency board arrangement, commercial banks do not compel exporters or service providers to convert export receipts into local currency or to maintain any percentage of proceeds onshore. For the 3D animation and VFX services export scope under ISIC 5911, a non-resident business corporation may retain 100% of export proceeds in offshore or domestic USD accounts and may freely repatriate funds. The applicable retention requirement is solely documentary: retention of the underlying commercial contract, invoice, and proof of service delivery for a minimum of five years to satisfy corporate record-keeping obligations under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, and production of this dossier to its RMI licensed bank or international correspondent bank upon request for AML/CFT source-of-funds verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability with strict legal constraints. Non-resident digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, and Mercury are not licensed passported entities in the RMI. They may onboard the MH_BC entity as a client only if they accept foreign-incorporated business corporations and their payment services operate through licensed partner banks with corresponding USD clearing in the U.S. federal wire system. The RMI Banking Act requires any entity conducting a 'banking business' in or from the RMI to hold a BMI license; however, an offshore EMI acting solely as a payment processor without maintaining a physical presence, soliciting deposits from RMI residents, or taking deposits in the RMI does not require RMI licensure and may operate as a non-resident service provider. Legal constraint: If the EMI holds client funds in a pooled omnibus account hosted by a U.S. or third-country bank, the MH_BC must ensure the EMI provides segregated sub-account identity protection, because the omnibus structure may undermine the MH_BC's ownership rights to funds and its ability to meet OFAC verification requests. Any EMI using the RMI jurisdiction code 'MH' is permitted, but if the EMI is, in turn, a U.S. Money Services Business (MSB), a U.S. state money transmitter license, must be verified. Wise and Airwallex currently support USD USD-denominated payouts to RMI entities with SWIFT routing via major U.S. correspondents; use is commercially recommended as a secondary clearing rail, but domestic bank onboarding remains the primary compliance anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for non-resident business corporations in the RMI. The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act does not require directors to appear physically before RMI banks or regulators. RMI licensed banks operating under the Banking Act and AML/CFT Regulations are permitted to conduct remote customer due diligence using a risk-based approach, provided that the bank undertakes reliable, independent digital identity verification, obtains certified true copies of incorporation documents from the RMI Registrar of Corporations, and completes enhanced due diligence (EDD) teleconference or video interview with at least two directors and the beneficial owner. In practice, the Bank of Guam and Bank of Marshall Islands will accept a U.S. notarized or apostilled corporate resolution, certified passport pages, proof of registered agent at Majuro or Ebeye, and a remote video interview if the beneficial owner's ultimate financing source is a reputable jurisdiction. However, physical presence at the bank's branch is effectively required if the corporate registry's apostille chain is incomplete or if any director or shareholder is tax resident in a high-risk jurisdiction. Recommended defense: maintain a registered agent with signing authority and a local director, or utilise 'remote banking onboarding plus local introducer' to remove mandatory travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director resident in a FATF grey-list / black-list jurisdiction or in a country with U.S. sanctions exposure, causing correspondent bank review failure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Beneficial ownership registry diagram from the RMI Registered Agent showing natural persons; 2) FATF-compliant source of wealth reports, sworn affidavit of lawful capital origin, audited financial statements of the ULTIMATE parent (if any); 3) OFAC/SDN screening clearance for each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner; 4) tax residency certificates for all beneficial owners; 5) a negative evidence letter from the bank's compliance team after enhanced background checks; 6) undertaking that no sanctioned counterparties will receive incoming or outgoing funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a U.S.-dollar account with unclear or pooled incoming funds from digital payment platforms (e.g., high volume of split payments from crowdfunding or distributed freelance remitters) without full remitter name and purpose code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) contractual service agreement for 3D animation work including detailed fee schedule; 2) itemised invoices with unique reference codes; 3) remitter-authorised payment records from Wise or SWIFT adopting the ISO 20022 remittance information field; 4) a business explanation letter describing the commercial CGI production cycle; 5) 12-month cash-flow projection showing payroll, software licensing fees (Autodesk, Unreal Engine, render farm), and subcontractor disbursements; 6) undertaking to supplement beneficiary name and address data for all incoming third-party payments within two business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payout to a personal account of a director in a different jurisdiction than the RMI entity's operational account, creating a perceived layering or tax evasion structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) director service agreement and legitimate expense reimbursement policy; 2) audited profit distribution resolution of the board of directors; 3) a run-rate model of residual profit distribution; 4) exchange-traded or quoted salary benchmark for CGI studio principals; 5) personal tax clearance certificates from the director's residence country; 6) internal controls requiring every dividend/payout to be recorded in the entity's general ledger with an independent approval timestamp; 7) third-party bookkeeping attestation (e.g., QuickBooks Online or Xero audit log) verifying that distributions align with declared financial year results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Required capital escrow account named 'Capital Escrow Account' for a non-resident BC with no minimum capital requirement, triggering classification as a high-risk special-use account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) legal memorandum quoting Section 28 of the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act confirming no minimum paid-up capital for BCs; 2) demonstration that the account is merely a segregated client deposit reconciliation account for production-related advances; 3) a copy of the underlying client production agreement; 4) letter from the registered agent validating the account is not a pooled client asset arrangement and that the MH_BC entity is the only beneficial owner; 5) ledger showing zero commingling of third-party funds; 6) agreement to reclassify the account as 'Operational - Prepaid Production Costs' upon request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce / 3D animation trade triggers under the U.S. Bank Secrecy Act controls on cross-border money laundering typologies because 'Animation & VFX' may be back-to-back license royalty payments not evidenced by 'real service'
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) detailed project chart of accounts for the 3D animation studio (line items for artists, render farm, software, storyboards); 2) production schedule per client; 3) behind-the-scenes asset renders or frame captures; 4) a sworn statutory declaration from the creative director confirming actual footage was generated; 5) contract with the downstream film distributor or broadcaster; 6) a third-party CPA letter confirming the service classification under ISIC 5911 and the arm's-length price.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Marshall Islands non-resident Business Corporation (MH_BC) engaged in commercial 3D animation production, inbound capital can be routed through SWIFT MT103 or through online payment rails (Wise, Airwallex) subject to proper source-of-funds documentation. Recommended structure: (1) equity/founder contribution: founder's personal or corporate US-based account sends a SWIFT MT103 wire to the MH_BC account at the Bank of Guam (Majuro) or Bank of Marshall Islands using SWIFT/BIC code 'BOMHMHMA' (if applicable) with purpose code 'T0201' (capital contribution) or 'G110' (other capital input) under ISO 20022; (2) project financing / client advance: client's corporate account wires via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'P0106' (services) and invoice reference; (3) production advance through Wise: fund laundering risk is mitigated by requiring the originator to include the actual client name and contract/purchase order number, and the RMI entity must produce the Master Service Agreement and the production budget. The Bank of Guam may treat wire transfers from 'higher-risk non-bank financial institutions' with enhanced scrutiny; therefore, the recommended rail is a first wire from the controlling owner's already-vetted commercial bank into the RMI account, followed by the EMI/neobank services after the relationship is established. The entity must verify the final beneficiary field in every wire matches the MH_BC legal name as recorded by the RMI Corporate Registry; any mismatch is a death-blow for clearing and will be returned after a 24-48 hour hold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for large supplier payments (CGI render farm farms, licensed 3D software procurement, payroll to overseas artists); (2) Commercial letters of credit are not needed for this service industry, but they may be used for pre-paid distribution licences, with MT700 between two commercial banks; (3) Wise Business multi-currency account ('Wise_B2B') for small-value disbursements under USD 25,000, using its local USD and EUR rails to pay overseas contractors; (4) SWIFT MT101/MT103 to a US correspondent, using the book transfer through Bank of Guam to settle USD in Fedwire or through CHIPS. Compliance requirement: every outbound disbursement must be supported by a pro-forma invoice and an internal treasury memo. Synchronise with the FX plan: all supplier contracts shall be denominated in USD; for non-USD payables (EUR, GBP, JPY), the RMI entity will execute a spot FX transaction via its bank or via Wise at point of disbursement, taking a clear 'benchmark price' screenshot for transfer pricing documentation. For amounts above USD 150,000, the bank will apply enhanced due diligence, requiring completed OFAC check on the payee and an invoice with an exact service description. Periodic shareholder distributions should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 with the purpose code 'T0110' (dividends) and underlying board resolution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: No RMI exchange control restrictions apply to hedging; the RMI uses USD so the MH_BC bears no USD/MH FX risk. However, the entity has material EUR/GBP/JPY exposure from international VFX clients. Permissible instruments: 1) vanilla FX forwards up to 12 months with a licensed U.S. or Asian bank (Bank of Guam, ANZ, Standard Chartered) under a standard ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement, only for forecast costs and receivables in the same currency; 2) non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible under the USD-displaced currency regime only if the underlying currency is the currency of client billing (EUR, GBP, JPY) and the counter bank carries an RMI-licensed or home-country AML/CFT regime; 3) cross-currency swaps with a maturity up to 24 months for funding of the production company's asset financing (e.g., render hardware leases), documented by an ISDA Schedule and CSA.

Instruments are not permissible: leveraged products, exotic/touch options, binary options, and any NDF linked to USD because USD is legal tender. Any hedging transaction must be excluded from speculative intent by a board resolution and documented by an internal treasury policy that ties notional values to forecast cash flows.

For the RMI entity, FX hedging shall be executed by a treasury service provider (e.g., Bank of Guam or a regulated U.S. futures commission merchant) that is not an RMI bank but that is permitted under the U.S. Commodity Exchange Act; the BMI has no restrictive licensing for non-resident derivative counterparties.
Currency swap accounting will follow ASC 815 / IFRS 9; the treasury management system or Excel log will tag hedge designations and valuations monthly.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report and Franchise Tax Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Corporate Registrar, Office of the Registrar, Majuro
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due on or before the last day of the month containing the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues USD 100 late fee plus USD 50 for each commenced month of delinquency; certificate of good standing is withheld; continued non-payment for more than two consecutive annual periods authorizes administrative strike-off and dissolution after 60 days' notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Audit and Corporate Records Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent, with inspection rights retained by the Marshall Islands Corporate Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed contemporaneously with the annual report, before anniversary month-end; updated within 30 days after any change in directors, members, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current registers is a Business Corporations Act default; Registrar may issue a compliance order and monetary penalty up to USD 1,000; repeated default supports corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Share Transfer UBO Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent as AML/CFT record-keeper (confidential; no public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each annual anniversary; within 14 calendar days after any share transfer that changes the beneficial ownership profile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML/CFT administrative penalty up to USD 25,000 per breach; the registered agent must freeze share-transfer registration and dividend payments until the beneficial ownership confirmation is complete.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a non-listed, non-resident Business Corporation; audit arises only where the Registrar orders an examination for suspected non-compliance or insolvency, or where shareholders holding at least 10% of the issued voting shares validly demand an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act fair-accounting standard; IFRS is the accepted international benchmark for non-resident entities; local GAAP is not separately codified.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information must be verified by the licensed registered agent at incorporation and re-confirmed annually at renewal; every share transfer must be accompanied by a revised beneficial ownership schedule within 14 days and before registration of the transferee, with a confirmation statement signed by the new ultimate beneficial owner or owners.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,200 per annum for a standard non-resident Business Corporation (registered agent, registered office, and annual report preparation support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000 only when a shareholder- or Registrar-directed audit is triggered; no routine audit cost applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective on foreign-source income of a non-resident Business Corporation; the RMI statutory corporate income tax rate of 3% of gross income applies only to income sourced within the Republic of the Marshall Islands and is not triggered by this entity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory 100% exemption of foreign-source income under the RMI Income Tax Act 1989; no capital gains tax, no alternative minimum tax, no branch remittance tax, and no gross receipts tax on export services; the exemption is automatic and requires no tax-holiday application or incentive filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NIL income tax return - the RMI Tax and Revenue Division issues no corporate income tax return to a non-resident Business Corporation deriving no RMI-source income; there is no electronic income-tax filing portal for such entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No statutory filing deadline applies because no return is due; were RMI-source income to arise, a return would be assessed by the Tax and Revenue Division on the 3% gross-income basis, and the BC would be required to notify the Division within 30 days of commencing RMI-source activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross receipts from Commercial CGI Visual Effects and 3D Character Animation services and IP licensing are excluded from RMI gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain service agreements, production contracts, and bank records proving that all personnel, servers, and performance sites are outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No penalty for the nil position itself; misreporting RMI-source revenue triggers the tax evasion sanctions detailed under fatal red flags (up to US$10,000 fine and 3 years' imprisonment).
